questions.question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

____ she was partly deaf, she was a gifted pianist.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option 2.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**although**" is used to introduce a contrast or concession between two statements. (हालांकि)
 
• In the sentence,** "Although she was partly deaf, she was a gifted pianist," **the word **"although"** appropriately introduces the surprising fact that despite being partly deaf, she had an exceptional talent.
 
• The other options: "**until**," "**because**," and "**yet**" do not fit the context as effectively.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

**Complete Sentence:** ***Although **she was partly deaf, she was a gifted pianist.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Until (जब तक)**: used to indicate the continuation of a state or action up to a certain point in time.
 
• **Because (क्योंकि)**: used to give a reason for something.
 
• **Yet (फिर भी)**: used to introduce something contrasting with what has just been mentioned, but less appropriate in this context compared to "although."

questions.question:

Morose
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Uplifted**.

• The word **"Morose"** means being sullen, gloomy, or in a bad mood. (उदास)

 
 
• **Example: **He became **morose** after hearing the bad news.

• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'morose' **is **'uplifted'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Uplifted**.

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect usage of the phrase "**too good for you to have**."
 
• The phrase **"too good" **typically implies something excessively positive, often leading to a negative consequence or implication, which seems out of place here.

questions.question:

questions.question:

Napoleon was one of the most capable generals in ____ history.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the omission of the article "**the**" before the term "**history**."
 
• Definite articles **("the") **are used to refer to something specific or known.
 
• In this context,** "the"** is appropriate because it specifies the particular history we are referring to.
 
• Thus, the correct sentence should be "Napoleon was one of the most capable generals in **the** history."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Napoleon was one of the most capable generals in **the** history."*

• **Option 3: "an"** – This article is indefinite and used before vowels, not applicable here.
 
• **Option 4: No article** – Omitting the article makes the sentence grammatically incorrect.
